mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 0.25% signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates for equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.25%, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 8.0% for three consecutive months, it signals weak labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 8.0% for three consecutive months, or Rank IC falls below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates broad consumer demand weakness that triggers negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced earnings expectations.
failure_condition: The interaction of declining HOUST and RSAFS fails to produce negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or Rank IC falls below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During manufacturing supply slowdowns (INDPRO growth rate below 0.5% annually), reduced production capacity and potential inflationary pressures cause negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO growth is below 0.5% annually, or Rank IC remains below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly real GDP expansion above 2.0% signals strong economic growth that boosts corporate earnings and investor confidence, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 growth exceeds 2.0%, or Rank IC falls below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When year-over-year CPI inflation exceeds 3.0%, it signals persistent inflation that may trigger premature monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL YoY exceeds 3.0%, or Rank IC remains below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) and increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates labor market deterioration that reduces household income and consumer spending, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction of declining PAYEMS and rising UNRATE fails to produce negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or Rank IC falls below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During housing market recoveries (HOUST growth rate above 2.0% annually), increased consumer confidence and spending drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to stronger retail sector performance.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST growth exceeds 2.0% annually, or Rank IC remains below 0.03.
